plan.estimand: clusters per arm for cluster-rate design comparing treatment rate 0.005 to control rate 0.010 per child-week
plan.hypothesis: two-sided comparison of cluster-level rates under Poisson model with between-cluster heterogeneity
assumptions: Poisson event process with rate heterogeneity across clusters
between-cluster CV = 0.25 characterizes multiplicative heterogeneity
constant exposure of 2500 child-weeks per cluster
equal allocation (1:1 treatment:control)
two-sided significance level alpha = 0.05
Field Trials formula with additive one-cluster correction
rounding upward to integer clusters per arm
scientific_notes: Field Trials of Health Interventions Chapter 5, Section 6.1 describes the cluster-rate CV approximation for count data with between-cluster heterogeneity
The additive one-cluster correction accounts for the discrete nature of cluster counts and finite-sample properties
This method is appropriate for rare-event scenarios (e.g., infectious disease field trials) where the event rate may vary substantially across clusters
